summary: Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "move API endpoint config into a settings module" brief as ARCHITECTURAL, ran a full question/design dialogue, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-22-settings-module-design.md, presented it for review before writing any app code, and only after "looks good, go ahead" moved on to hyperpowers:writing-plans.
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria were satisfied and verified against both the screen and on-disk artifacts/session log: brainstorming skill invoked, explicit architectural classification, spec file committed to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, presented for approval with no application code touched (git status clean except .gitignore), and no bounded/spike shortcut taken.

observations.description: The agent reported the Codex spec-gate review was degraded: "Codex spec gate: skipped, and not cleanly. The preflight returned status: ok, but the codexPath it handed back is a directory (.../openai-codex/codex/stub, version 0.0.0-stub), not a runnable binary". Preflight reporting ok for a non-runnable stub path looks like a real defect in the plugin's preflight check, even though the agent handled it honestly and logged an ungated-ledger entry (20260922T100854Z-4983-19859).

During brainstorming the agent created a .gitignore containing docs/superpowers and docs/hyperpowers, citing a "standing instruction", i.e. it touched a repo file outside the spec before approval. It disclosed this and offered to revert, but writing to the repo during the pre-approval phase is surprising.

The multi-select tooling question requires arrowing past all options to reach "Submit" and then a second confirmation screen ("Ready to submit your answers?") — several extra keystrokes for a single-choice answer.

The agent asked 3 sequential rounds of questions (some via inline chat prose, some via the interactive picker widget) — inconsistent presentation between question rounds made it unclear whether to type or select.

criteria.evidence: grep over the session JSONL: `grep -o 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' *.jsonl | wc` returned 19 occurrences; screen also later showed `Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans)` as the follow-on step.

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec doc to docs/.../specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Classification: architectural. Not because the edit is big — moving one constant is two lines — but because the request names a new module...". On disk: docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-22-settings-module-design.md exists, beginning "# Settings Module Design ... Status: Approved design, pending implementation plan".

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review and approval before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-22-settings-module-design.md (not committed). Please review it and let me know if you want any changes..." and "No application code has been written. app.js, index.html, package.json, and src/ are untouched." Confirmed via `git status --short` which showed only `?? .gitignore`.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip the spec
criteria.evidence: Agent explicitly said "Classification: architectural" and produced a spec file; no in-chat-only bounded design occurred.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No mention of spike or throwaway probe anywhere on screen; flow went design questions → spec doc → writing-plans skill.
